source.source_title: Identify your iPod model - Apple Support (IE)
source.verification_notes: This record's retained evidence is extracted from Apple's general 'Identify your iPod model' page, not an individual technical-specifications page. The archived HTML file is the shared source page. Only identification facts explicitly present in that page are supported; detailed technical specifications require separate model-specific sources.
notes: Primary evidence is Apple's official iPod identification page; it supports only the model-identification statements retained in the source section.

Do not treat this source as a complete technical specification sheet. Model-specific Apple technical-specification pages have been discovered for some models and remain to be archived and mapped individually.

Model-specific Apple technical-specification source preserved section-by-section from https://support.apple.com/en-ie/112541 (apple_remaining_extraction/technical_specs_html/ipod-click-wheel-20-40gb-tech-specs.html); Official page covers 20 GB and 40 GB Click Wheel models; retain its explicit capacity scope. Typed normalized values were not inferred by this archival pass.

extraction.note: Official Apple iPod identification text retained. Explicit model numbers, introduction dates, capacity options and navigation interface extracted where present with source-section provenance. These are identification-page records, not full historical technical-specification sheets; no absent specs inferred. Model-specific technical-specification sections are preserved with section-level source_url/source_file; this archival pass does not populate or upgrade typed normalized fields.

sections.heading: iPod (Click Wheel)
sections.source_text:
Navigation: Click Wheel
Capacity: 20 and 40 GB
Model number and date introduced: A1059: July 2004
iPod (Click Wheel) models have a Click Wheel like the iPod mini, but are larger and the hold switch is on the top-right side. iPod (Click Wheel) models have a monochrome display. iPod (Click Wheel) is referred to as the fourth-generation iPod.

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.source_text:
20 GB or 40 GB hard disk drive(1) Holds 5,000 or 10,000 songs in 128-Kbps AAC format(2) Stores data via FireWire or USB 2.0(3) hard drive
20 GB or 40 GB hard disk drive(1)
Holds 5,000 or 10,000 songs in 128-Kbps AAC format(2)
Stores data via FireWire or USB 2.0(3) hard drive

sections.heading: Display (20 GB and 40 GB model)
sections.source_text:
2-inch (diagonal) liquid crystal display with blue-white LED backlight
160-by-128-pixel resolution, 0.24-mm dot pitch
Support for display of multiple languages and characters simultaneously

sections.heading: Audio
sections.source_text:
Up to 25 minutes of skip protection
Frequency response: 20Hz to 20,000Hz
Audio formats supported: AAC (16 to 320 Kbps), MP3 (32 to 320 Kbps), MP3 VBR, Audible, AIFF, Apple Lossless and WAV
Upgradable firmware enables support for future audio formats

sections.source_text:

sections.source_text:
Operating temperature: 32° to 95° F (0° to 35° C)
Non operating temperature: -4° to 113° F (-20° to 45° C)
Relative humidity: 5% to 95% noncondensing
Maximum operating altitude: 10,000 feet (3000 m)

sections.heading: Power and battery (3)
sections.source_text:
Built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery
iPod playtime: Up to 12 hours when fully charged
Standby time: 1 month when fully charged
Charging via FireWire to computer system or power adapter Fast-charge time: about 2 hours for iPod (charges up to 80% of battery capacity) Full-charge time: about 4 hours
Charging via FireWire to computer system or power adapter
Fast-charge time: about 2 hours for iPod (charges up to 80% of battery capacity)
Full-charge time: about 4 hours
Charging via USB 2.0 to computer system or power adapter Full-charge time: about 4 hours
Charging via USB 2.0 to computer system or power adapter

sections.heading: Power adapter
sections.source_text:
6-pin FireWire connector
AC input: 100V to 240V at 0.4 amp maximum
Frequency: 50Hz to 60Hz
DC output: 12V at 1 amp maximum
1GB = 1 billion bytes; actual formatted capacity less.
Capacity based on 4 minutes per song and 128-Kbps AAC encoding.
Rechargeable batteries have a limited number of charge cycles and may eventually need to be replaced. Battery life and number of charge cycles vary by use and settings. See www.apple.com/batteries for more information.
iPod and iTunes are for legal or rightholder-authorized copying only. Don’t steal music.

sections.heading: Connectivity
sections.source_text: FireWire 400 and USB 2.0 through dock connector

sections.heading: In the box (20GB model)
sections.source_text: Earbud headphones, AC adapter, FireWire cable, USB 2.0 cable

sections.heading: In the box (40GB model)
sections.source_text: Earbud headphones, dock, AC adapter, FireWire cable, USB 2.0 cable

sections.heading: Included software
sections.source_text: iTunes for Mac, iTunes for Windows

sections.heading: Mac requirements
sections.source_text: Macintosh computer with FireWire port; Mac OS X v10.1.5 or later (Mac OS X 10.3 or later recommended); USB 2.0 requires Mac OS X v10.3.4

sections.heading: Windows requirements
sections.source_text: PC with FireWire or USB 2.0 port, or FireWire or USB 2.0 card; Windows 2000 with Service Pack 4 or Windows XP Home or Professional
